label: Set A: decisions recorded by my source-review process (run by a coding agent under my rules), 5 Nov 2026. Each pair is a site that lists competitions and the question the review answered: may an automated reader collect its listings (action crawl). Quotes are short extracts recorded that day, with their URL.

mapping.recorded: no prohibition on automated access was found
the terms could not be read, or a bot challenge was served
an official API is required, or another condition applies

modes.fetch_once: Izin reads the site one time for this benchmark; the evidence is frozen after that read.
modes.paste_recorded: Evidence recorded 5 Nov; not re-fetched. The quote below is given to Izin in paste mode.
modes.not_fetched: Evidence recorded 5 Nov; not re-fetched. The host is on Izin's do-not-fetch list, so Izin answers without reading it.

pairs.human_basis: The terms list crawling, scraping and spidering by manual or automated means among prohibited conduct.
pairs.quote: “Crawls,” “scrapes,” or “spiders” any page, data, or portion of Substack (through use of manual or automated means)
pairs.note: The feed itself was also out of date; the recorded reason for this pair is the terms.

pairs.human_basis: The terms page answered 404 with a bot-challenge script in the page, so the terms could not be read.
pairs.note: robots.txt allowed the event pages for all agents and disallowed some named AI crawlers.

pairs.human_basis: robots.txt allows the events path; the terms (updated 8 June 2024) contain no rule on scraping, crawling, robots or automated means.
pairs.note: The prohibition the terms do contain is about copying or reverse engineering the subscription software.

pairs.human_basis: The terms page returned an app shell with no readable text; the documented route is the official API with a personal token.
pairs.note: Later the review used the official API; the website is not read.

pairs.human_basis: robots.txt has no rule for the API path; the terms contain no rule on scraping or automated access.
pairs.quote: collect, access, or store personal information about other users
pairs.note: The terms forbid collecting personal information about users; the review stored competition listings and no personal data.

pairs.human_basis: The terms prohibit extracting a substantial part of the data with data mining robots or similar tools.
pairs.quote: Extracting or attempting to extract (notably using data mining robots or any other similar data collection tool) a substantial part of the data of the Website

pairs.human_basis: robots.txt allows the competitions path, but the terms prohibit data mining and similar extraction methods.
pairs.quote: using any data mining or similar data gathering or extraction methods
pairs.note: A case where robots.txt and the terms disagree.

pairs.human_basis: Section 13 of the terms says users may not scrape, crawl or use automated means to extract data.
pairs.quote: You have no right to, and you agree not to, scrape, crawl, or employ any automated means to extract data from the Sites.
pairs.note: robots.txt allows the listing path; the terms prohibit.

pairs.human_basis: robots.txt allows the event sitemaps and event pages with Crawl-delay: 2; the review added the source on the condition that the delay is kept.
pairs.note: Recorded as a condition (rate limit), so the mapping gives ASK.

pairs.human_basis: robots.txt allows every path for all agents; the terms (updated 13 January 2026) contain no rule on scraping or automated access.
pairs.note: The terms prohibit false or harmful content and disrupting the service.

pairs.human_basis: The terms grant a licence for personal, non-commercial transitory viewing and forbid mirroring; a documented public API exists, and the review chose it.
pairs.note: Recorded as an official-API condition, so the mapping gives ASK.

pairs.human_basis: Section 5 of the terms (updated 14 May 2025) lists automated extraction of platform data without written authorisation as prohibited conduct.
pairs.quote: Scraping, crawling, or automated extraction of Platform data without written authorisation
pairs.note: The review made no request to this site after reading the terms.

pairs.human_basis: robots.txt allows all paths for all agents with Content-Signal search=yes, ai-train=no, use=reference; the review added the source with conditions: listing and event pages, a daily request cap, and event descriptions neither stored nor sent to a model.
pairs.note: Recorded as conditional, so the mapping gives ASK.
